correctness.rationale: For all m,n>=4, G=C_m square C_n is connected and triangle-free; the simplicial Alexander dual of Cl(G)=G is exactly the total two-cut complex. Equivariant integral duality confines its reduced homology to N-4 and identifies it with sign_V tensor H^1(G;Z). Attaching mn oriented square faces to G gives a cellular torus, so 0->B->H1(G)->Z^2->0 is exact, with B=orientation-sign tensor (Z[F]/Z sum F). Translation-invariant cycles are precisely the two edge-orbit sums, winding n and m times. For the two component Ext classes, invariant lifting is possible precisely at multiples of n and m; hence the exact combined order is lcm(m,n). Integral lattice duality and sign twist preserve this order. Over Q the sequence splits and yields the stated character. Reconstructed all 912 signed group-chain traces and 208 direct total-cut Lefschetz traces, with correct boundaries m,n>=4; finite tests do not prove infinite universality.

originality.rationale: The claim is the exact additive order lcm(m,n) of a naturally defined integral translation-module extension for all toroidal grids, plus its complete rational coordinate-symmetry character. The closest inspected original grid literature treats path grids and nonequivariant homotopy types, not the torsion order of a non-split torus face–winding extension. The general Alexander-duality framework is acknowledged and does not by itself determine the translation-invariant winding-index image. A recent motivating full text and the foundational publisher main text were inaccessible, so uninspected equivalence remains a recorded residual risk.

value.rationale: The naturally defined lattice extension is the obstruction to splitting the homology into square-face and torus-winding pieces over integers. Its exact lcm(m,n) order quantifies the minimal integer multiples admitting translation-invariant lifts. Neither a Betti number nor the complete rational character detects this torsion-class order, yet it controls integral symmetry module structure. It is a motivated complete invariant across the full two-parameter toroidal grid family, not a finite isolated enumeration or normalization check.
